text:
Filip Forsberg went from a slow start to the center of Nashville's revival; Sports Illustrated ran it as "How Filip Forsberg Broke out of his Slump and Saved Nashville's Season." His two goals in a 3-0 win in Los Angeles came in the middle of a seven-game winning streak, and he has 24 points in 22 games.

His own shooting is honest. Eight goals on 7.57 expected (the quality of his chances) is right where it should be. The issue is everyone else around him. Nashville has scored 12.9 more goals than its chances deserve with Forsberg on the ice, and it is padding his assist total. The Predators are under 50% of 5v5 shot attempts with him out there, so this is a team getting results ahead of its process.

Evolving-Hockey had last season the other way around: his expected wins well above his actual, the chances there without the finishing. Maybe this is the bill coming due in his favor. Either way, at 32 he is still a volume shooter with a heavy release, 92nd percentile in top shot speed. Our numbers say the assists are the part to watch.
headline: Forsberg's points carry a luck tax
